# Appeal of Denial — Knee Arthroscopy / Meniscus Surgery (CPT 29881)

**RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination**
**Member:** Avery Lawson
**Member ID:** W601208268
**Plan:** MedStar Family Choice DC (Commercial/ACA), District of Columbia
**Denial Date:** 2026-08-06
**Reference Number:** POC-0948C5760B-46622
**Governing Policy:** Utilization Management Criteria — https://www.medstarfamilychoicedc.com/-/media/project/mho/mfcdc/medical-policies-and-procedures/policy-115dc_utilization-management-criteria.pdf

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of my knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery (CPT 29881), which was denied on 2026-08-06 with reference number POC-0948C5760B-46622. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking the plan to reconsider its decision.

## Why I believe this denial should be reconsidered

The denial notice states that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I want to walk through what my records actually show, because I believe they do support this surgery.

- I have had 24 months of progressive knee pain that has not improved with rest.
- I completed 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy (20 visits, 2026-03-10 through 2026-06-30) focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion. This is documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- I used NSAIDs for 6 months without adequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-26 gave me only 2 weeks of partial relief.
- My MRI from 2026-05-28 shows a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking.
- I experience locking and giving way in the knee, cannot squat or kneel, and am limited to walking on level ground.
- My exam findings include positive provocative testing on the affected side and pain-limited range of motion.
- I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I do not smoke.

Given a displaced, locking meniscal tear that has not responded to months of physical therapy, medication, and injection, I do not understand how the plan concluded that my imaging does not support medical necessity, and I am asking for that conclusion to be reviewed again in light of the full record.

## The plan's own policy on criteria

The Utilization Management Criteria policy that governs this decision states:

> "MedStar Family Choice DC follows documented UM criteria to facilitate consistency in UM decision making across all service types."

It also states:

> "All criteria utilized in utilization management are available upon request."

and

> "To request specific utilization management criteria or to speak with a Medical Director, please contact us by phone during our normal business hours, 8:00 AM to 5:30 PM, Monday through Friday at 1-(855)-798-4244."

I have not been given the specific clinical criteria that were applied to my case — only these general statements that such criteria exist and are available on request. I am not able to fully evaluate whether my records were measured against the right standard without seeing that standard, and I do not believe I should have to guess at it.

## My request for the specific criteria applied

I understand that MedStar Family Choice DC, like many health plans, may use InterQual criteria, which is licensed software rather than a publicly posted document. I am formally requesting, in writing, that the plan provide me with **the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination**, or, if some other clinical criteria were used instead, the specific criteria document and section applied to CPT 29881 in my case. Under federal ERISA and ACA appeal rules, I understand I am entitled to receive this information free of charge as part of my appeal.

## Deadline and where I am sending this appeal

I understand my appeal must be received by 2027-02-02. I am sending this letter to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, or, if that is unclear, to the address confirmed by calling the number on the back of my insurance card and asking where member appeals are filed.

## What I am asking for

I am asking MedStar Family Choice DC to:

1. Reverse the denial of CPT 29881 (knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery) and approve this procedure; and
2. Provide, in writing, the specific criteria (including the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text, if applicable) that were relied upon in reaching this denial.

Thank you for reviewing this appeal. Please contact me if any additional information is needed.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Avery Lawson
Member ID: W601208268
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
Date: [date of submission]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
